rv.q: It’s a magnificent piece of acting that makes you almost nostalgic for a vanished gestural style.
Altogether this is a highly recommended foray into a murky, neglected chapter of our theatrical and national history.
‘Adrian Lester reprises his award-winning performance, bringing an intriguing chapter of theatre history to life.’
This display of phenomenal talent makes the injustice of his fate truly wrenching, though its power is rather sapped by the spoilerific, essentially redundant framing device.
Adrian Lester gives an eye-wateringly good performance as Aldridge, full of peppy vigour when he arrives in Covent Garden, ready for the future.
Nevertheless, Aldridge is an incomplete protagonist, and too many aspects of his life are told to us, rather than shown.

cn.t: Critics widely praise *Red Velvet* as a powerful, timely revival, with Adrian Lester's performance called definitive and grandeur-filled. Chakrabarti's script on racial prejudice resonates strongly.
